text:
kevin: Heads-up — we're seeing a correlated spike in east-west p99 for GPU inference pods in eu-west1 starting ~08:07 UTC. p95 ok, but p99 jumps ~120ms. Network graphs show bursts of TX drops on several hosts. :thinking_face:

cassie: Which qdisc are those hosts on? Any recent kernel or tc changes rolled?

kevin: Looks like a recent infra change last night to add a root HTB + fq_codel rootclass to enforce burst policing (to limit noisy-tenant flows). I pulled `tc qdisc show dev eth0` from one affected host:

```
root@node-317:~# tc qdisc show dev eth0
htb 1: root refcnt 2 r2q 10 default 12 direct_packets_stat 0
    qdisc fq_codel 10: parent 1:12 limit 1024 quantum 1514 target 5ms
```

maria: fq_codel itself is usually fine, but if somebody applied aggressive `limit`/`quantum` or combined with ingress policing it can cause reordering/drops seen by RDMA or GSO-heavy flows. Are these hosts using RDMA or offloads?

kevin: Some of the GPU hosts have Mellanox NICs with mlx5 kernel driver. RDMA is enabled for CUDA-aware MPI jobs, but inference pods shouldn't use RDMA. I ran `ethtool -k eth0` and saw TSO/GSO were still on (as expected). Also saw `tx_timeout` and some `tcp_retrans` spikes in netstat.

infra-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-227 — "eu-west1 intra-cluster p99 spike". Pager duty notified (on-call: cassie).

cassie: Can we reproduce on a single host pair? I can run an iperf3 + small gRPC-ish flow to measure. Also let's check MTU mismatch — that sometimes wakes up when offload+qdisc interacts. `ip link` on host?

kevin: `ip link show eth0` shows mtu 9000. One of the edge leaf switches had a config rollback overnight to 1500 on a subset of ports due to a vendor bug fix. So partial MTU mismatch is plausible. That + fq_codel might force fragmentation at kernel layer and break GSO -> lead to increased CPU path and reorder.

ben: Yikes. MTU mismatches + offload toggles are a classic perf footgun. Suggestions: 1) revert rootclass shaping to previous config (canary on 2 hosts), 2) temporarily disable fq_codel on affected hosts, 3) disable TSO/GSO as a last resort for troubleshooting (not a long-term perf win).

maria: Also check `sysctl net.core.default_qdisc` and `net.core.rmem_max/wmem` — some workloads assume big buffers. If fq_codel is dropping aggressively and buffers small, it will raise retransmits.

kevin: Running quick checks on node-317 and node-318 now. `tc -s qdisc show dev eth0` shows a lot of `drops` and `requeues` on node-318. node-317 (canary) has much lower drops; looks like node-318 is on the rollback switch port (MTU 1500).

cassie: I'm going to: 1) move a small canary inference deployment to node-317/319 (both 9000 MTU) and run synthetic load to compare p99; 2) disable the new rootclass on node-318 and observe. I'll update in ~10m. :eyes:

david: If MTU mismatch is the root cause, we should also check RDMA/ib devices — when IP over RDMA or encapsulation happens, the kernel might behave differently. `rdma link` and `ibdev2netdev` could show mapping.

cassie: Canary results: node-317 p99 ~ 18ms under load, node-318 p99 ~ 150ms with retries. After removing the rootclass (tc qdisc del dev eth0; re-add plain ifb-less qdisc), p99 on node-318 dropped back to ~20ms. No change to ethtool offloads yet.

kevin: So interaction between MTU mismatch + rootclass fq_codel shaping appears to have amplified fragmentation/reassembly and triggered retransmits impacting latency. Good catch.

ben: Plan: 1) Roll back the rootclass change across eu-west1 hosts for now. 2) Run a host audit to find any switch ports with non-9000 MTU and either fix at network layer or add targeted host exceptions. 3) Add a preflight check to infra deploy that verifies uniform MTU + NIC offload compatibility for hosts with fq_codel. 4) Postmortem with timeline + suggested kernel/driver config.

maria: Also add a monitoring alert for sudden increases in `tc drops` or `tx_dropped` on host NICs so we can trigger faster.

kevin: I'm doing the rollback rollout script now (canary -> batch). Will post updates. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Status update posted to #INC-2026-227.
